subject: Silverline: evaluation window, throughput uplift & pilot commercial
messages:
From: Mike Lang <mike.lang@silverlinehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluating Redwood for scale + cost — next steps

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a short internal comparison between Redwood and a competitor (NimbusAI) against a subset of our production prompts. High level: Nimbus came in slightly better on nominal per-token cost for our 1k–2k token prompts, and their p95 latency looked ~20% lower under the same VM sizes.

We still prefer Redwood’s operational model and the routing/fallback story, but before our execs sign off we need:
- A short performance window (48–72h) where we can validate latency and throughput on our real workloads.
- Assurance we can scale to ~2x our current Q4 baseload during the pilot (we’ll provide traffic shape).
- A commercial outline to compare vs the competitor (pricing + term tradeoffs).

Can Redwood commit to running a focused benchmark next week and give a firm pilot pricing for a three-month proof with dedicated capacity?

Also attaching a one-page summary of the internal benchmark we ran (high-level numbers).

[Attachment: silverline_benchmark_summary.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

GL,
Mike Lang
Head of Platform Engineering
Silverline Health

--
This is a commercial evaluation — procurement will want timeline and SOC2 artifacts if we move forward (cc procurement@silverlinehealth.com).

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Mike Lang <mike.lang@silverlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-11T12:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood for scale + cost — next steps

Mike — really appreciate the clear ask and for sharing the summary. Short answers up front: yes, we can run a tight validation window and stand up dedicated capacity for the pilot; we just need to align on success metrics and traffic shape.

Proposed plan (high level):
- 72-hour validation window next Tue–Thu (May 16–18). Redwood will provision a dedicated test pool (same GPU family as production), route a representative traffic replay you provide, and collect p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost.
- Success criteria: p95 latency < 250ms for your 1–2k token prompts, and sustained throughput at 2x Q4 baseline for at least 60 continuous minutes during the window.
- Commercial: 3-month pilot on dedicated capacity. Initial proposal: 15% off list for pilot with an option to convert to a 12-month committed capacity contract (tiered commits) — we’ll firm up numbers after the run.

Attached is a quick test-plan draft that Naomi and Marissa helped pull together. If that looks good we’ll schedule the run and Naomi will pull SOC2 and audit artifacts for procurement.

Next steps:
1) Confirm dates and provide traffic replay / sample prompts by EOD Friday.
2) Naomi to share SOC2 and evidence pack.
3) Ben to drop a provisional commercial term sheet post-run.

[Attachment: redwood_test-plan-v1.pdf (DOCX, 85KB)]

Thanks — I’ll block time with the team and start provisioning if you confirm the window.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
On 2028-05-11 09:12, Mike Lang wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a short internal comparison between Redwood and a competitor (NimbusAI) ...

From: Mike Lang <mike.lang@silverlinehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@silverlinehealth.com
Date: 2028-05-12T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood for scale + cost — next steps

Evelyn — thanks, that plan is sensible. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock dates:
- p95 < 250ms is critical. Our internal baseline target is 200–250ms. If you can demonstrate sub-250ms at the stated token lengths, that addresses most of the exec concerns.
- We will need the ability to simulate bursts to 2x Q4 baseline (these are predictable scheduled bursts tied to vendor batch jobs).
- Procurement timeline: procurement will expect a commercial anchor by May 25; they also asked for SOC2 Type II report and a list of sub-processors.

One other data point: the competing vendor is offering ~20% off list with a 12–18 month commit. We may not take the discount, but it sets the bar in the evaluation.

I can provide a traffic replay and our prompt set by Friday. If you can confirm commitment to the run by EOD today we’ll lock the dates.

Best,
Mike

[Attachment: procurement_timeline.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Mike Lang <mike.lang@silverlinehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood for scale + cost — next steps

Mike / team — appreciate the transparency on competitive terms. I’ll keep this short and practical so procurement has something to compare.

Commercial bridge we can offer for the evaluation:
- 72-hour dedicated validation window (no charge for the run).
- Pilot pricing: 15% off list for a 3-month dedicated pilot (as Evelyn noted).
- Convert option: If you convert to a 12-month committed capacity within 30 days of pilot completion, we’ll apply an additional 7% credit for the months already paid during pilot (effectively stacking into a 22% total first-year discount).
- Operational commitments: guaranteed canary region failover, two-week runway for capacity increases, and a joint runbook for fallback to cheaper model variants in the event of sustained utilization.

We’ll need a signed mutual action plan to lock these terms (simple doc) and a PoC acceptance ticket to capture the success criteria. I’ll drop a HubSpot note for SL-4829 with the above and a draft MAP. Link: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/SL-4829

If procurement needs SOC2 artifacts immediately Naomi (cc) can drop the evidence pack today.

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Ben's mobile: (415) 555-0192

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-15T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Silverline run coordination + ask list (do not externalize yet)

Team — quick coordination note before the run next week. This thread has the external context above; callouts below for engineering/ops: 

- Naomi: please share SOC2 Type II PDF + sub-processors list with procurement today (linked to the deal record). Procurement wants the artifact ahead of the run.
- Marissa: we need a canary config (model variant with quantized weights) + fallback policy. Goal is to show that under a 2x burst we can drop to a lower-cost variant with <5% quality delta for a short window. Can you prepare a test candidate and the instructions we’ll use during the 72-hour window?
- Ops (Ben / infra): provision a dedicated pool sized for 2x Q4 baseline and the ability to ramp. Please also enable token-level tracing (per-request latency headers) and provide access to trace logs for Silverline engineers.

Logistics:
- Traffic replay file and prompt set to be uploaded to the Drive link by EOD Friday.
- Naomi to post SOC2 zip to the HubSpot attachment and procurement@silverlinehealth.com.
- Ben to publish the draft MAP and pilot SOW to the HubSpot record (SL-4829).

I’ll sit on the run with the Silverline SREs and coordinate status reports. If we can get the p95 under 250ms in the first 24 hours that will materially change the commercial conversation.

Thanks — please confirm when each owner has completed their piece.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference> replied: "On it — SOC2 package uploaded, will share link by EOD."
